Here are the latest dated announcements and news, including SEC filings, for Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS), onsemi (ON), Wolfspeed (WOLF), and Astera Labs (ALAB) as of today, **October 12, 2026**:

### **Astera Labs (ALAB)**

*   **October 12, 2026:** Astera Labs unveiled Orion, a modular rack-scale reference design engineered for AI infrastructure, allowing customers flexibility in choosing GPUs and CPUs. This design features a 320-lane PCIe switch fabric capable of connecting up to 160 accelerators per pod. Orion is expected to be available through Astera Labs' ODM and OEM partners starting in Q1 2027 and will be showcased at the 2026 Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit.
*   **October 12, 2026:** Astera Labs, in collaboration with Lumentum and Corning, announced a joint demonstration of PCIe-over-optics connectivity for AI rack-scale architectures at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. This demonstration will combine Astera Labs' Scorpio Smart Fabric Switch with Lumentum's 1060 nm VCSEL-based optical interconnect platform and Corning multimode fiber connectivity.
*   **October 12, 2026:** A Form 4 SEC filing indicated that director Craig H. Barratt was granted restricted stock units (RSUs) on **October 1, 2026**, as non-employee director retainer fees. These RSUs are scheduled to vest on the three-month anniversary of **August 15, 2026**.
*   **October 7, 2026:** A Form 144 SEC filing indicated that affiliate Stefan A. Dyckerhoff proposes to sell 12,499 common shares.

### **Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS)**

*   **October 12, 2026:** Navitas Semiconductor introduced its new 24 kW, 800 V-to-12 V DC-DC power delivery board, utilizing GaNFast™ technology. Developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, this board supports the NVIDIA MGX ecosystem and is designed to advance 800 VDC power architectures for AI data centers. It is slated for display at NVIDIA's AI Factory MGX Wall partner area during the OCP Global Summit 2026.
*   **October 6, 2026:** Navitas completed the acquisition of Claros, Inc., integrating Claros' integrated voltage regulator (IVR) technology into its portfolio. Navitas anticipates this acquisition will contribute at least $3.5 billion to its identified 2030 serviceable available market (SAM). A Form S-8 was submitted on this date.

### **onsemi (ON)**

*   **October 12, 2026:** onsemi unveiled advanced semiconductor packaging technology aimed at enhancing the efficiency of EV inverters. This new architecture is designed to enable higher power density, reduce electrical losses, and simplify power-system integration, contributing to smaller and more efficient traction inverters for electric vehicles.
*   **October 10, 2026:** onsemi's broad product price adjustment, announced on **September 16, 2026**, officially took effect. The company cited ongoing increases in raw material, manufacturing, energy, and infrastructure costs, alongside heightened demand in power, industrial, and data center applications, as reasons for the adjustment.
*   **October 1, 2026:** onsemi and Synaptics Incorporated announced an amendment to their merger agreement, transitioning the transaction to an all-cash deal. Under the revised terms, onsemi will acquire Synaptics for $123 per share, valuing the deal at approximately $5.7 billion. This change followed an unsolicited competing acquisition proposal received by Synaptics. The transaction is expected to conclude by mid-2027. An 8-K SEC filing was made on this date.

### **Wolfspeed (WOLF)**

*   **October 12, 2026:** Wolfspeed and GEENER Microelectronics entered into a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on silicon carbide power module solutions. GEENER intends to prioritize Wolfspeed's silicon carbide bare dies for its next-generation power module platform, initially targeting traction inverters for new energy vehicles. Future expansion plans include AI data centers, industrial power supplies, and energy storage.
*   **October 8, 2026:** The US Department of War extended a conditional loan offer of up to $1.5 billion to Wolfspeed over 30 years, in exchange for warrants allowing the department to purchase up to 7.5% of the company. This financing is earmarked to bolster US production of silicon carbide materials and power devices, with a strategic focus on national security applications. The first installment of $600 million is intended to repay senior secured notes due in 2030.
*   **October 7, 2026:** Wolfspeed submitted a Form 8-K SEC filing.
